output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes mainly from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency nurses. The hardware move was meant to be like-for-like. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules, including the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-alarm suppression, and routing of probe-off alerts to the charge phone only. The tool still reported success. Pods A-C phone notifications per nurse per shift roughly doubled, from about 38 to about 80. Acknowledgement times doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, shows no change. Alarms generated by the monitors stayed flat, so acuity and the September monitor update are unlikely causes. Delayed-response rates rose equally for core, agency and new-graduate nurses on Pods A-C, and Pod D agency staff showed no rise. Disciplining nurses and capping agency use would punish the wrong group and would not fix the cause. Recommendation: restore the 11 skipped rules, with clinical validation and committee sign-off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Decline the proposed performance reviews. The sick-leave link is plausible but unproven, since respiratory illness was also rising hospital-wide. Confidence is high on the main cause.
